newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Aluminium seen drifting lower on LME - trade.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium seen drifting lower on LME - trade.

text.p: Aluminium prices are tipped to slip lower later on Tuesday on the London Metal Exchange (LME) due to technical selling while Chinese buyers may find copper prices increasingly attractive, base metal traders said.
"I see the selling continuing this afternoon. Aluminium may drop to US$1,540 (a tonne)," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading company said.
"There may be more technical selling to come as the chart picture is not inspiring. Nearby support is pegged around $1,550 and then $1,535," broker Brandeis said in its daily review.
Brisk two-way trade in aluminium was seen by Singapore base metal dealers.
Three-month LME aluminium was seen by the trade reaching as high as $1,589/94 a tonne at 0200 GMT before profit-taking knocked the price back to around $1,585/90 a tonne around 15 minutes later.
Aluminium was indicated in the LME late on Monday at $1,583/85 a tonne.
One dealer said aluminium's fall should be limited and the metal should be underpinned by good demand from Japanese carmakers and the construction industry.
"Demand is rising in those two sectors," a Japanese dealer said.
Another dealer said aluminium should range between $1,565 and $1,610 a tonne when the LME opens later on Tuesday.
Copper prices, on the other hand, are seen dropping lower on further fund selling and are beginning to reach levels which may soon attract Chinese buying, dealers said.
"It seems there's some interest from the Chinese side, but nothing major so far," a dealer for a European metal trading company said.
A Japanese dealer said the price of the red metal should hold between $2,280 and $2,300. He said: "I think the Chinese will start buying at some point. They feel this would be a good price to buy."
Brandeis was less optimistic about the red metal's price.
"Technically, although some support should be found around $2,250, we cannot discount a move to more solid support at $2,200 particularly as the indicators turn lower," it said.
Three-month copper was quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at $2,272/72 a tonne against the late London quote on Monday of $2,270/74 a tonne.
LME copper stocks are seen dipping by about 3,000-4,000 tonnes when the stocks report comes out at 0800 GMT, dealers said. Aluminium stocks are tipped to also fall by 5,000-6,000 tonnes.
The trade is watching the inflow of zinc into the LME's Singapore warehouse after 6,000 tonnes were placed on warrant last Friday, bringing the total volume of zinc here to 13,825 tonnes.
"I think the bulk of the zinc which arrived here has been placed in the LME," a zinc dealer said.
Traders estimate about 2,000-5,000 tonnes of zinc from China is bound for Singapore and should arrive within the next two weeks.
